entities.name: The Adventures of Tom Bombadil
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Adventures of Tom Bombadil is a 1962 poetry collection by J. R. Tolkien, creating a lasting cultural footprint in the realm of fantasy literature.

This collection was part of Tolkien's broader legacy as a scholar and linguist, particularly his work on Old English and Middle English.

As one of the most celebrated works of the 20th-century fantasy genre, it has influenced numerous authors and adaptations, including The Lord of the Rings film trilogy.

Its impact can be seen in the proliferation of Tolkien-inspired fiction, from children's books to adult novels, as well as its influence on the development of fantasy role-playing games.

The Adventures of Tom Bombadil also exemplifies the blending of mythology and historical context, reflecting Tolkien's interests in European folklore and cultural heritage.

In 2013, a 50th-anniversary edition was published, featuring a revised introduction by Christopher Tolkien.

Tolkien's use of Middle English created a unique linguistic style that has been studied and emulated by scholars and language enthusiasts alike.

The collection's enduring popularity can be attributed to its imaginative storytelling, memorable characters, and the sense of wonder it evokes in readers.

Its significance extends beyond literature to the realm of cultural iconography, with Tom Bombadil becoming a recognizable figure in popular culture.

As a product of Tolkien's scholarly expertise, The Adventures of Tom Bombadil remains an important example of the intersection between academic knowledge and creative expression.
